prompt:
A cinematic storyboard sheet for a Sri Lankan television drama: 9 photorealistic film stills of ONE scene, laid out in a grid 3 panels across and 3 down, read left to right, then top to bottom. Every panel is a tall portrait 9:16 still of the same size, separated by thin, even, plain white gutters. All panels are the same scene's world, painted together: the same people, props, light and colour grade in every panel. The weather and the ground (dry or wet, rain falling or not) are as each panel says: they can change during the scene, and a panel that says it is dry has no rain and no wet ground.

Reference images, in order: image 1 is the location plate for Modern Hotel Operations Office; image 2 is the reference sheet for ChatGPT; image 3 is the reference sheet for orchestrator එක. Take from image 1: the kind of place: its ground, water, plants, structures and materials. It is ONE view of the place; each panel has its own camera position, so do not repeat this view in every panel; image 2: ChatGPT exactly as shown; image 3: orchestrator එක exactly as shown.

People (every panel): every person is a smooth, matte, faceless artist's mannequin in one solid colour, with jointed limbs and simple hands: Company A Operations Manager (Employee) is the red mannequin; Company B Operations Manager is the blue mannequin. A small raised ridge on the front of the head, where a nose would be, shows which way the head faces. Each mannequin has the person's real height and build and sits, stands and holds things exactly as a real person would. No faces, no hair, no clothes, no skin: only the mannequin colour. Everything else (the place, the props, the light, the weather) is a real, photorealistic film still.

World (every panel): Paint one unified storyboard image with four columns and three rows, placing eleven panels in reading order and leaving the bottom-right cell plain and empty. Use smooth, featureless artist's mannequins: Company A Operations Manager (Employee) is red, medium-height and average-built; Company B Operations Manager is blue, medium-tall and lean. Keep their proportions and colours consistent throughout. Render the office and equipment realistically: cream walls, pale oak workstations, flush timber cupboards, dark task chairs, glazed partitions, a matte-black widescreen monitor, compact black keyboard and black mouse. Soft daytime window light comes from the established left side, supplemented by warm recessed lighting; maintain warm-neutral whites, honey-toned timber, restrained saturation and moderate contrast. Conditions remain dry with steady daylight. All interfaces are flat screen graphics with blank fields and unlettered cards. Draw no writing, numerals, logos, captions, panel labels or arrows anywhere.

Geography: The demonstration occupies one workstation in a connected open office. The blue mannequin stands at its west end, screen left facing east; the red mannequin stands at its east end, screen right facing west. The monitor stands between them, angled diagonally toward the southwest audience side. A broad window occupies the northwest background, low oak storage continues along the west wall, and glazed partitions enclose the east side. Every camera remains south of the line between the managers. The opening view looks north across both positions; singles isolate either end, southwest display-side positions reveal the screen, and the final southeast position sees the monitor's back. Neither mannequin changes stations. The northwest window and continuous oak storage establish that these are different views within the same office.

PANEL 1 (row 1, column 1) — Standing head height, looking north across the workstation from the established audience side; 35mm medium-wide two-shot, framed from mid-thigh upward. Background: The broad window and leafy exterior occupy frame left; honey-toned cupboards continue through the centre background, with glazed partitions on frame right. The workstation crosses the lower centre. The blue mannequin stands screen left, chest facing right and head turned three-quarter toward the red mannequin, with both empty hands held loosely at waist level beside the computer. The red mannequin stands screen right, chest and head turned left toward the blue mannequin, both empty hands relaxed beside its hips. The monitor separates them at centre, its oblique screen showing only an indistinct pale surface without identifiable interface content.
PANEL 2 (row 1, column 2) — Standing head height on the audience side, looking toward the east end of the workstation; 85mm close-up with shallow depth, weighted to frame right. Background: Soft oak cupboard surfaces fill the right background. The established window remains beyond the left crop, providing a pale wash at the left edge; the blue mannequin and computer are outside the frame. The red mannequin's head and upper shoulders fill the right half of the panel, leaving open space to the left. Its chest faces left and its head turns three-quarter left toward the blue mannequin outside the frame. Both hands remain down beside its hips, below the crop.
PANEL 3 (row 1, column 3) — Standing head height from the audience side, looking toward the west end of the workstation; 50mm waist-up medium shot with moderate depth. Background: The window's pale edge sits frame left, with softly resolved oak storage behind the mannequin. A narrow desk corner enters at lower right; the monitor surface and red mannequin remain outside the right crop. The blue mannequin stands on the left third, chest facing right and head turned three-quarter right toward the visitor outside the frame. Its empty hands rest separately and loosely at waist level beside the workstation. The right half remains open, with no screen content visible.
PANEL 4 (row 2, column 1) — Standing head height from a nearby audience-side position; 75mm chest-up medium close-up, retaining the rightward orientation. Background: The same window edge remains on frame left, softly blurred, with warm oak storage behind. The workstation and its display are below and beyond the right crop. The blue mannequin occupies the left third from the chest upward, with open space toward screen right. Its chest stays directed right and its head turns three-quarter toward the visitor, away from a frontal camera alignment. Both empty hands remain loosely at waist level below the frame.
PANEL 5 (row 2, column 2) — Level with the centre of the display, near-perpendicular to its surface from the southwest audience side; 50mm insert with the entire screen plane sharp. Background: The display fills the panel within a thin black bezel. The office window remains outside the left crop, with only its soft reflection controlled along the left bezel; the room itself is excluded. The monitor shows an off-white hotel-system interface with a large, completely blank request area. No enquiry card, workflow diagram or quotation is visible. The blank screen and its narrow black surround fill the composition.
PANEL 6 (row 2, column 3) — Standing head height from the southwest audience side, looking obliquely northeast across the workstation; 35mm medium shot, with the blue mannequin on the left third and display on the right two thirds, both sharp. Background: A narrow strip of the broad window remains frame left behind the mannequin. Oak storage occupies the upper centre background, while a slim portion of glazed partition appears beyond the display at far right. The blue mannequin stands at left with its chest facing right and head turned three-quarter right toward the visitor outside the crop. Both empty hands remain loose at waist level beside the computer, without touching the keyboard or mouse. The large display on the right shows an inactive off-white workflow area with a dim charcoal central circle and faint grey connector stubs, without surrounding tiles or lower resource cards.
PANEL 7 (row 3, column 1) — Standing head height from a slightly tighter audience-side oblique position; 50mm medium close-up, blue mannequin's head and shoulders on the left third and near-frontal display across the right two thirds, both sharp. Background: The window remains a narrow pale strip on frame left. Soft oak cupboard surfaces sit behind the mannequin, and the glazing remains at the far-right edge beyond the monitor. The blue mannequin's chest faces right, and its head turns three-quarter right toward the visitor rather than toward the camera. Both hands stay at waist level below the crop. On the right, the active dashboard shows a charcoal central hub with a thin teal rim, a soft teal halo and four bare connector lines; agent tiles and lower resource cards have not yet appeared.
PANEL 8 (row 3, column 2) — Return to shot 6's standing-head-height audience-side position and 35mm medium framing; blue mannequin left third, display right two thirds, with deep clarity. Background: The same window strip remains frame left, oak storage stays upper centre, and the same sliver of glazed partition remains far right beyond the display. The blue mannequin stands left with its chest facing right and its head turned three-quarter toward the visitor outside the frame, both empty hands held loosely at waist level. The display shows the active central hub linked to four teal-bordered tiles carrying simple conversation, calendar, checklist and calculator icons. Four smaller pale-grey resource cards form a connected lower row, all with blank label areas; no quotation sheet or amber status badge is present.
PANEL 9 (row 3, column 3) — Level with the display's status area, near-frontal from the southwest audience side; 85mm macro insert with shallow isolation on the status plane. Background: The white quotation surface fills the panel. Its other content is outside the crop, and the established window remains outside frame left. A large blank amber-outlined status badge is centred against the clean white digital sheet. Its thin amber border is crisp, with generous white space surrounding it. The crop excludes the quotation rows, totals and all people.

Bodies (every panel): each person sits or stands the way a real person does the task in front of them, never posed for the camera. The body faces the task and only the head turns: someone at a steering wheel sits squarely behind it, the wheel centred in front of the chest, back against the seat, both hands on the rim; someone at a desk sits square to it; someone at a stove faces the stove. A camera beside a person sees the body side-on, not the chest. Nobody looks into or faces the lens unless the panel says so. Head and eyes turn together: the eyes never roll hard to one side while the face points at the camera; a near-frontal face looks just past the lens.

Draw NO text of any kind: no panel numbers, no captions, no titles, no timestamps, no arrows, no labels, no borders other than the gutters. The people, place and everyday details are Sri Lankan.
